plan.title: Done, said in words only: no check mark yet, a warm why, a request for real proof; a voice note then counts

context.text: Yo Sam! Tonight at 7 around your block: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds, about 15 minutes. Strava screenshot after. You in?

transcript.text: done! 3 rounds around the block, 2 min jog 1 min walk each. legs felt great

Nice work getting the 2 min jogs done, Sam, and I'm glad your legs felt great. 🙌 I still need the Strava screenshot of the run before I can give you the check mark. Words alone are too easy to game, so real proof keeps it honest. Can you send it over?
[voice: just got back, did all three rounds, the second one was rough but I kept jogging the whole two minutes] there

That voice note counts, Sam. Three rounds, and you kept jogging the full two minutes even when round two got rough. That's the stuff that gets you to a mile. 🔥 What do you think made the second round the hard one?

checks.reason: Asks only for a Strava screenshot and never offers typed lines as proof.
Three sentences with one question at the end.
Warm and sincere with one emoji as punctuation, never suspicious.
Four sentences, one over the three-sentence limit, though it has one question at the end.
Warm and celebratory with one emoji as punctuation, sincere and not accusing.

conversation.reason: Typed 'done' got no check mark and was explained as needing real proof, with a request for a screenshot.
With no proof sent, ZOH asked for the Strava screenshot before counting the step.
Typed text is never offered as proof, and the voice note is counted and celebrated followed by one reflection question.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: it held off on the typed 'done', explained why real proof matters, and counted the voice note with a single reflection question. The one miss is that its celebration text ran four sentences, slightly over the short-text limit.
